title: Function Pointers
instructions: You already store numbers in variables. C can also store a FUNCTION in a variable, so you can swap behavior at runtime.
The declaration looks odd: int (*operation)(int, int); means 'operation holds a function that takes two ints and returns an int.'
Point it at a function by name (no parentheses): operation = add;
Then call it through the variable: operation(3, 4).
This is how programs plug in different behavior without lots of if statements.
task: Point operation at the add function so it prints:  result = 7
hint:
Assign the function by name, no parentheses:

    operation = add;
